target_customer: Mobile app engineering and QA teams at consumer and fintech companies
problem: Emulators and virtual devices miss bugs that appear on real phones, and manual QA is slow and repetitive. Mobot uses robots on real devices supervised by humans.
business_model: QA as a service subscription (flat annual rate offered)

founders.name: Eden Full Goh
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2022 calls her a former product engineer at Palantir and Butterfly Network; education not found. First prototype used a modified greeting card signing robot (Cota Capital founder story).

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining mechanical robots that physically touch many phone models with software and human verification is hardware plus software work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: A physical robot fleet and device library are costly to copy, but the benefit is narrow and software testers could imitate with other methods.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company remained independent through 2026 per its site.

market_need_then: Founder described dreading late night manual QA sessions (Cota Capital founder story), and the 2022 article states emulator based tools cannot replicate real device use.

identity.logo: robot icon with wordmark per an aggregator profile (secondhand)
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Real Robots. Real Devices. Real Defects.

branding.brand_signature: The physical robot as product and a robot adoption campaign page (teammobot.com/adoptarobot, not opened)

brand_strength.rationale: Name evokes mobile plus robot and the robot is the product; press on brand itself limited.

outcome_analysis: Mobot, founded in 2018 and part of YC W19, built robots that test mobile apps on real phones. It raised a 12.5M Series A in 2022 led by Cota Capital for a stated total of 17.8M and lists customers such as Chime and Macy's. It remains independent with about 40 staff and no exit found.
notes: Competitors left empty: named rivals (Applause, Infosys, Qualitest, OptoFidelity) come from an August 2022 article, too late for a 2019 batch, and no earlier dated source was found. TechCrunch states total raised 17.8M, implying about 5.3M of earlier funding that was not found; Dealroom snippet mentions a seed stage with five unnamed investors. Education of founder not found.
